notes: BL1 is not named in the brief; it is included as the predecessor that carries the published NIST lifetime result (2005, revised 2013) and because BL2 is described in sources as largely the same apparatus.

physics_goals.quote: One method of determining the free neutron lifetime involves the absolute counting of neutrons and trapped decay protons.
physics_goals.value: Determine the free neutron lifetime by absolute counting of neutrons and trapped decay protons in a cold neutron beam

summary.plain: The first of the NIST beam-method measurements of the neutron lifetime. It counted the decay protons from a cold-neutron beam trapped in a magnetic and electric field and, with a better calibration of the neutron counter in 2013, gave a lifetime of 887.7 seconds.
summary.technical: NIST BL1 beam neutron lifetime (2003 measurement, reported 2005): neutron-decay protons trapped in a Penning-type proton trap in a superconducting solenoid and counted against the absolute neutron fluence; revised in 2013 with a directly calibrated 6Li neutron monitor to tau_n = 887.7 ± 1.2 stat ± 1.9 syst s.
